Miqaat is a prayer clock. It calculates the five daily prayer times on this device for the place you choose, plays the azaan, and can count down to iqamah for prayer at home.  Nothing is uploaded: there is no account, no advertising and no analytics. Two things use the network — the optional place-name lookup (Android's geocoder, run by Google) and the update check on GitHub in the direct-download edition. Both are off until you use them.

These windows are conservative estimates (after Fajr until sunrise, ≈15 min after sunrise, ≈10 min around zawāl, after ʿAsr until sunset); the texts describe events, not minute counts, and schools differ on the details. The three solar windows: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 831; after Fajr and after ʿAsr: Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī 586. Obligatory prayers are not restricted by them; a missed prayer is prayed when remembered (Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 684), though schools differ on doing so inside these windows.
